issues.issue: "Design of a full campaign plan" states no content, deliverable or completion standard, so what would discharge the obligation is undefined. The introductory promise that the scope "clearly defines" the services is in tension with so open-ended an item.

The deliverables are introduced by "Including:", leaving open whether the enumerated communications tools are exhaustive or merely illustrative of a larger duty. Terms such as "proof points" and "weakness inoculation" have no fixed meaning.

"[A]ll branding, digital and other needed collateral materials" pairs a general catch-all with two specifics, leaving the reach of "other needed" materials uncertain. Who decides what is "needed" is not stated.

"[A]s needed such as voter issue mapping or focus groups" leaves the reach of the research obligation to be inferred from two examples. Whether Xenophon merely recommends or must procure the research is also unclear.

This sentence conditions all third-party research billing on client approval, while section 4.2(c) requires prior approval only for Third-party Expenses of $1,000 or more. The two approval regimes cannot both govern research costs below that threshold.

"Undertake education activities to inform them" sets no measurable content or volume, and "them" depends on the antecedent in the preceding sentence. What counts as performance cannot be fixed from the words.
A national "breakout" story is an undefined and unmeasurable objective, and "on-going news stories" sets no frequency. The clause states an aspiration rather than an ascertainable duty.

"[B]est efforts" is undefined and the provision supplies no benchmark against which placement efforts could be measured. The disclaimer that placement "is not guaranteed" leaves the residual obligation to be construed.

"[K]ey publications" has no defined boundary, and the promise "to write and place op-ed columns" sits against section 1.1's acknowledgment elsewhere that placement is not guaranteed. Neither the number nor the identity of publications is fixed.

"[A]s necessary to groups likely to support the Client's efforts such as the U.S. Chamber of Commerce" attaches a single specific example to an open general class. The extent of the outreach duty cannot be determined from the words.
"[B]uild a relevant audience" specifies no size, platform or metric, so performance is unmeasurable. "[O]ne or more platforms" leaves the scope entirely to the promisor.
"[P]eriodic monitoring" fixes no interval and "rapid response" no time limit. The frequency of the promised service is therefore indeterminate.

"Other communications tasks as agreed upon by the client" is an unbounded catch-all closing a list of specific services, so its reach against the enumerated items is uncertain. Whether such tasks fall inside the retainer or outside the Scope of Services turns on this phrase.

This open-ended item cannot easily be squared with section 1.2, which charges services "that fall outside the boundaries of the Scope of Services" at hourly rates; work agreed under "Other Tasks" is simultaneously inside and outside the scope. The boundary between the two provisions is left unresolved.

"Xenophon's then-currently hourly rates" refers to a rate schedule that appears nowhere in the Agreement, and the phrase is itself garbled. "[S]uch as public affairs campaigns" gives one example for an otherwise unbounded category of "[a]dditional services".

This hourly-rate billing regime sits against section 4.1, which fixes a $30,000 monthly retainer for the scope of work, and against 1.1's "Other Tasks" catch-all; nothing identifies which regime applies to a given task. The Agreement contains no rate card to make 1.2 operable.

"[W]ill be on-going" fixes no term or end date, leaving the duration of performance indeterminate; the section is also misnumbered 2.4 in an Article whose only other section is 2.2. The absence of any 2.1 or 2.3 compounds the uncertainty about what was intended.

An "on-going" period of performance must be read with section 2.2, which permits either party to terminate on 60 days' notice; whether the contract is perpetual or terminable at will is left to be harmonised.

"[T]erminated by either party with 60-days written notice" does not say when notice is effective, whether the retainer accrues through the notice period, or what happens to work in progress. The measure of "60-days" against the monthly billing cycle is unstated.

This right to terminate must be reconciled with section 2.4's "on-going" period of performance and with section 6.1, which lets the Client stop all work while still paying "in accordance with the terms and provisions of this Agreement". Whether stopping work under 6.1 avoids the 60-day notice is unresolved.

"[W]ill include but is not limited to" names six individuals while disclaiming that the list is exhaustive, so the staffing commitment has no ascertainable content. Nothing states any minimum involvement by the named personnel.
"[S]imilarly qualified" is undefined and supplies no criteria (seniority, experience, rate) for judging a substitution. Whether the Client has any say is not addressed.

"[D]uring or for a period of one year following the conclusion of this Agreement" does not say whether "conclusion" means expiry, termination under 2.2, or completion of work. "[O]ffers of employment" is also undefined as against hiring an applicant who approaches the party.

The sentence is grammatically tangled: "any individuals then-currently employed by the applicable Party during the term of the Agreement either directly or through a third party" mixes a present-tense reference point with a term-long window, so the covered class is uncertain. It is unclear whether "through a third party" describes the employment or the offer.

"[D]amages equal to one year of the employee's gross salary" does not say whose salary figure governs — the old employer's or the new one's — or at what date it is measured. Whether this liquidated sum is the exclusive remedy is also unstated.

The section fixes a flat "monthly retainer of $30,000 plus expenses" yet also requires Xenophon to "track all hours and supply full detail", leaving it ambiguous whether the retainer is earned regardless of hours worked or is a draw against time actually spent. "[S]ubject to a possible calendar year price increase not to exceed 5%" further leaves unclear who may impose the increase and when.

The requirement to supply full hour detail "along with them monthly invoices" conflicts with section 5.1(a), under which "[a] detailed summary of billable time will be provided to the client the following month, after it is incurred". The two provisions set different times for the same deliverable.

"Incurred routinely in conducting its work" is an undefined qualifier that does not mark the boundary of reimbursable Out-of-Pocket Expenses. The defined term "Expenses" is introduced here but the subparagraphs then use different labels.

The 6% is computed on "the professional fees contained in the Client's monthly Invoice", but the Client issues no invoice under this Agreement — Xenophon does — so the computation base is misdescribed. It is also unclear whether the flat 6% replaces or supplements actual charges in the listed categories.

Section 5.1(a) re-describes this same charge as "the six percent professional fee outlined in section 4.2 (a) ('Out-of-Pocket Expenses')", conflating an expense allowance with a professional fee. The two descriptions of the same item do not match.

The parenthetical "(i.e., transportation, lodging, meals and related expenses)" purports to define "non-local travel" but repeats "meals", which are already a separate head, and adds an open "related expenses". "[A]uthorized by the Client" does not say whether authorisation must precede the expense or in what form.
